newsitem.title: MEXICO: US stocks can withstand more rate hikes - NYSE VP.
newsitem.headline: US stocks can withstand more rate hikes - NYSE VP.

text.p: U.S. equity markets can withstand further interest rate hikes, given investors' increased appetite for stocks, James Cochrane, senior vice-president of the New York Stock Exchange, said Wednesday.

"The equity markets in the United States can easily absorb modest increases in short-term interest rates, given the extraordinary, growing appetite on the part of U.S. persons and people from outside of the United States to purchase equities," he told a news conference at a conference on emerging markets. "There is a tremendous demand to buy equity securities."
Cochrane added, "The flow of money is quite strong and it can easily overcome any negative effect of an increase in short-term interest rates."
He said a bulge in the population of people 40 to 55 years old, many whom are saving for the first time, is propelling much of the investment in equities.
"We are now expecting to live longer," he said.
He said the policy-making Federal Open Market Committee rarely lifts interest rates only once, preferring instead a series of rate hikes.
The Federal Reserve increased the federal funds rate by 25 basis points on March 25, the first hike in about two years. The FOMC is to meet again on May 20.
Cochrane said countries such as Mexico are also unlikely to be seriously affected by modest U.S. rate hikes.
